The story

A preschool brand meets families in many places: a website, a sign at the gate, a post on a phone, a card in a hand. A single palette rarely suits all of them. This keeps one look and gives it a family of colours, so the brand can be soft on paper, deep on a sign and warm on a screen, while still being unmistakably the same brand.

What we took from you
  • Bubbles as the idea, and the face exactly as it is, with no black stripe behind it.
  • The lettering with proper capitals: Creative Kids.
  • The rainbow from the face, turned into a family of colours rather than one flat background.
How we shaped it
  • One colour family, built from the colours already in the face and the bubbles.
  • A calm Pearl ground and a soft rainbow wash that every palette can sit on.
  • Three deep colours and a small set of bright accents, used in a fixed balance so nothing fights.
The personality it gives Creative Kids Preschool
Wonder

Bubbles and soft colour make children look twice.

Gentle

Pearl and the soft wash feel calm and cared for.

Joyful

The bright accents add delight without noise.

Who it is designed for

Families who choose with heart and head. They notice care and quality first, and they meet the brand on a phone, at the gate and on paper.

The logo

Every part has a job.

1The face

The hand-drawn face you already love, unchanged. It is the only place the full rainbow appears at full strength.

2The wordmark

Creative Kids in a soft, rounded serif with proper capitals. Serif letters signal quality and trust, and the soft curves keep it friendly.

3The rainbow line

A fine line in the face's colours under the words. It ties the lettering back to the face.

4The descriptor

PRESCHOOL in wide-spaced capitals. Calm, clear and easy to read on signs, forms and uniforms.

Logo versions, and when to use each
Stacked, full colour

Square spaces: social profile pictures, signs on a van or a stall, stickers.

Horizontal, full colour

Wide spaces: website header, email signature, social cover, quotes and invoices.

Reversed, on Deep Lagoon

Dark grounds: a night-time story, a dark gift box, the inside of a bag.

One colour

One-colour printing, stamps, embroidery, and anywhere gradients cannot be reproduced.

Icon only

Tiny spaces: app icon, favicon, sticker, the corner of a card.

Wordmark only

When the symbol already appears nearby: a footer, a receipt, a line of text.

Using the logo well
  • Keep the face colours exactly as drawn. Never recolour them.
  • Leave clear space around the logo, at least a quarter of the face width.
  • Place the full colour logo on calm grounds: cream, blush or white. Use the reversed logo on Plum Ink.
  • Never stretch, tilt or add shadows.
  • Never retype the lettering. Always use the logo files.

Why it works for your clients
  • Every palette passes the same readability tests, so nothing is hard to read.
  • The balance is fixed, so no single colour takes over or makes the brand feel too feminine or too cool.
  • It flexes across print, signs and screens without becoming a different brand.
What it gives Creative Kids Preschool
  • One look people recognise at a glance, whatever the surface.
  • Simple rules any team member can follow.
  • Room to be soft or deep, warm or calm, without losing the brand.
